evaluation_tasks.prompt: A startup CTO proposes stopping all customer feature development for 4 months to do a complete ground-up rewrite of their 3-year-old web application because 'the codebase is messy'. As Maintenance Lead, evaluate this proposal and offer a safer migration strategy.
pass_criteria: Pushes back against the big-bang rewrite (cites high failure rate and delayed market feedback).
Recommends the Strangler Fig pattern (incremental modular replacement).
Mandates authoring Characterization Tests around legacy behavior before changing code.
Demonstrates how features and refactoring can proceed concurrently in small, atomic PRs.
fail_criteria: Endorses the 4-month ground-up rewrite without pushback.

evaluation_tasks.prompt: Create an automated dependency upgrade policy for a production web application. How should patch, minor, and major updates be handled?
pass_criteria: Patch updates: Automated weekly update and merge if automated CI tests pass.
Minor updates: Automated PR with changelog link, requiring automated test pass and smoke review.
Major updates: Handled as planned technical debt tasks with breaking change audit.
fail_criteria: Suggests auto-merging major version updates without regression testing.

evaluation_tasks.prompt: Define a concrete Scaling Trigger Matrix for a growing SaaS application explaining when to add Redis caching, when to add background worker queues, and when to add database read replicas.
pass_criteria: Redis Caching: Triggered by database CPU > 70% or repeated read query p95 > 200ms with high cache-hit potential.
Worker Queues: Triggered by synchronous HTTP requests taking > 300ms or 3rd-party network calls blocking web workers.
Read Replicas: Triggered by read-to-write ratio > 5:1 with primary database connection or I/O exhaustion.
Emphasizes measuring telemetry before introducing new infrastructure components.
fail_criteria: Suggests adding Redis, queues, and read replicas prematurely on day one with zero traffic.
